points.t: Small **dark red, purple or black papules** on the scrotum or vulva, a limb, or **clustered between umbilicus and knees**.
**Dilated papillary dermal capillaries** with thickened epidermis; **Fabry disease** is X-linked α-galactosidase A deficiency.
Reassure typical Fordyce lesions; dermoscopy (dark lacunae); refer a solitary dark lesion if doubt; **enzyme / genetic testing** for possible Fabry.
**Melanoma mimic**; **Fabry** with burning hand / foot pain, kidney, heart and stroke risk.

cause.lead: Dilated vessels under a warty surface.
points: Ectatic papillary dermal vessels + reactive epidermal thickening.
**Angiokeratoma corporis diffusum** (many, bathing-trunk) → lysosomal storage disease: classically **Fabry** (GLA gene, Gb3 build-up in vessels, kidney, heart, nerves); also fucosidosis, sialidosis.

visuals.caption: Angiokeratoma: blood-filled dilated vessels just under a thickened epidermis give a small dark red-purple papule.
visuals.alt: Skin section with dark blood spaces under thick epidermis

points: **Solitary / multiple**: adults, legs; dark red-black: **can mimic melanoma**.
**Fordyce**: older men (scrotum), women (vulva); multiple small purple papules; may bleed.
**Mibelli**: children / teens, dorsal fingers and toes; chilblains.
**Corporis diffusum**: bathing-trunk → **Fabry**: childhood **acroparaesthesia** (burning hands / feet with heat, exercise, fever), **hypohidrosis**, proteinuria, cardiac / stroke.
If a dark lesion could be melanoma.
α-Gal A activity (males); **GLA gene test** (needed in females); plasma lyso-Gb3; urine protein, eGFR, ECG / echo.

manage.lead: Reassure, refer the doubtful, test the pattern.

points: Reassure isolated angiokeratomas; treatment is cosmetic (laser, cautery, excision; not NHS-funded).
Uncertain dark lesion → refer (dermoscopy / biopsy); NG12 urgency if 7-point ≥ 3.
Bathing-trunk angiokeratomas, neuropathic pain, sweating problems, proteinuria or early cardiac / stroke history → **Fabry testing**.
National lysosomal storage centre: enzyme replacement (agalsidase alfa / beta, pegunigalsidase alfa) or oral **migalastat** (amenable mutations); cascade-screen family.

limits.t: Every other day; no food 2 h before and after.

items.t: Many angiokeratomas in a child / young adult with burning hand / foot pain, reduced sweating or proteinuria: test for **Fabry**.
Solitary changing dark papule you can’t confidently call an angiokeratoma: **possible melanoma**.

pearls.t: Bleeding scrotal Fordyce lesions are benign, but **ask about other symptoms** (patients are often embarrassed).
Burning hands in childhood + reduced sweating + bathing-trunk papules = think Fabry.

quiz.a: GLA gene testing (enzyme may be normal).
No food 2 hours before and after; every other day.
